transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is that I’m having trouble with eating at night. It’s not just that I snack more than I should — it’s like once I start, something sort of takes over. I can be standing there thinking, very clearly, “Stop. You don’t need any more. Put it away.” And at the same time, my hands are still reaching for more food.

It’s a strange feeling, because I’m aware of it while it’s happening. I’m not confused or anything. It’s more like I’m watching myself do it, almost from the outside, and I’m arguing with myself in my head, but I don’t actually stop. That’s the part that scares me a bit, honestly. It feels like I’ve lost the steering wheel once it gets going.
Do you feel that this nighttime eating is something you have to do to relieve a feeling of tension or anxiety, or do you fear something bad will happen if you don’t eat that way?

I’m not sure it’s like that, exactly. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there thinking, “If I don’t eat this, something terrible is going to happen.” It doesn’t feel like that kind of fear, at least not that I’ve noticed.

There is tension sometimes, I guess, but I don’t know if the eating is to relieve it in a clear way. It’s more like… once the thought is there, and the food is there, it starts feeling very hard to interrupt. But I’m not aware of any specific anxiety that builds up beforehand, and I don’t have a belief that I have to do it to prevent something bad. It’s more confusing than that.
Do you feel like you have to eat in a certain way, such as eating specific foods, in a certain order, or for a certain reason, once you start eating at night?

I don’t think so… not in the sense of rules or a ritual, if that’s what you mean. Like, I don’t have to eat things in a certain order, or only eat one particular food, or chew a certain number of times or anything like that.

It’s more scattered than that, honestly. Sometimes it’s whatever is easiest to get to, or whatever happens to be there. I might start with one thing and then move to something else, but it doesn’t feel planned or organized. I’m not thinking, “First I need this, then I need that.” It’s just… once I’ve started, I keep going, and the choices feel kind of automatic.

I also don’t know that there’s a particular reason in my head, like a rule I’m following. I’m not trying to make something “feel right,” exactly. It’s more like I get pulled along by it, and afterward I can look back and think, “Why did I even eat that?” But during it, it’s not a structured thing. At least, I haven’t noticed a pattern like that.

Do these nighttime eating episodes feel completely involuntary to you, like they happen automatically without any real choice on your part, or do you feel like there’s still a part of you that’s choosing to continue eating even if you wish you could stop?

I wouldn’t say it’s completely involuntary, like my body is moving and I’m not there at all. I am there. I can see what I’m doing. That’s actually part of what bothers me so much — I’ll be thinking, very clearly, “Stop now. That’s enough. Put it away. Go upstairs.” And then my hand just goes back into the bag, or I open the fridge again, or I take something else out.

So there must be some part of me choosing, I guess, because I’m physically doing it. But it doesn’t feel like a normal choice. It doesn’t feel like when I decide what to have for dinner or decide to make coffee. It feels more like I’m watching myself continue even though the better part of my mind is saying not to.

It’s like the stopping part doesn’t connect to the doing part. I can be almost arguing with myself while it’s happening, and the eating just keeps going. So no, not completely automatic, but not really under control either. That’s the best way I can describe it.
Before these nighttime eating episodes start, do you usually feel a growing sense of inner tension, urge, or discomfort that seems to be relieved by beginning to eat?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed it that clearly. I’m trying to think back to right before it starts, and it’s not usually like there’s this obvious pressure building in my chest or this strong anxiety where I can say, “Okay, now I need to eat and then I’ll feel better.” It’s not that neat.

Sometimes I’m just kind of restless, or tired, or my mind is wandering, and then the idea of food comes in. But I can’t honestly say I’ve connected it to a specific inner tension that rises and then gets relieved the moment I start eating. Maybe there is some discomfort there and I’m just not very good at noticing it, but if you’re asking what I’m aware of, it’s more like the eating starts before I’ve really identified any feeling.

Once I begin, there can be a sort of… I don’t know, narrowing of focus, like now I’m in it. But I’m not sure I’d call that relief. It’s more that I stop thinking about whether to do it and just start doing it. So I don’t want to say no completely, because maybe there’s something underneath, but I haven’t recognized a clear pattern of tension first and relief after starting.
Do you feel any sense of pleasure or satisfaction while eating during these nighttime episodes, or does it feel more neutral or even unpleasant?

I’m not sure I can give a clean answer to that. I mean, there are moments where it tastes good, of course. I’m not going to say I’m completely unaware of taste or that it’s all horrible from the first bite. Sometimes the first few bites are… not exactly pleasurable in a happy way, but there’s something satisfying about them, like, “Okay, I’m eating this now.”

But it doesn’t stay like that, if that makes sense. It becomes less about enjoying it and more about continuing. The taste almost fades into the background. I’ll still be eating, but I’m not savoring it the way I would if I were sitting down to a meal I actually wanted. It can get kind of mechanical.

And then there are times where, even while I’m eating, I’m already uncomfortable with it. Not physically necessarily right away, but mentally. Like I know I don’t really want to be doing it, so the pleasure is mixed with this heaviness or frustration. I might still keep eating something that doesn’t even taste that good anymore, which is embarrassing to admit, because then it’s obviously not about enjoyment in the normal sense.

So I’d say it starts with maybe a little satisfaction sometimes, but a lot of the episode feels pretty neutral, or even unpleasant in my head. It’s not like I’m sitting there having a good time. It’s more like I’ve gotten pulled into it, and any pleasure is brief and then gets swallowed up by the feeling that I can’t quite stop.

Do you ever feel driven to eat at night because of intrusive, unwanted thoughts or mental images that keep coming into your mind, where eating feels like the only way to get rid of those thoughts or reduce the discomfort they cause?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing it. I’m trying to be careful because I don’t want to miss something, but I wouldn’t say I have some specific thought or image that keeps barging in and then eating is the only way to make it go away.

It’s not like there’s a picture in my head or a phrase repeating over and over that I’m trying to neutralize, if that’s what you mean. I don’t usually think, “If I eat this, that thought will stop.” It’s more muddled than that. Sometimes my mind is busy or I’m tired or sort of drifting, but I haven’t noticed a particular unwanted thought that drives the whole thing.

There can be thoughts about food, obviously — like knowing something is downstairs, or remembering what’s in the cupboard — but that feels different from an intrusive thought. It’s more like the idea of eating becomes hard to step away from, not that I’m trying to get rid of some disturbing image or mental noise.

So I’d say no, not really. Or at least not that I’m aware of. If there is discomfort beforehand, I don’t experience it as “I have to eat to get this thought out of my head.” It’s more like I get pulled toward eating without a clear reason I can point to.

Do you ever feel a strong, almost irresistible urge or compulsion to start eating at night, even if you're not hungry, where it feels like the need to eat takes over your thoughts completely once it begins?

Yes… that part does feel true. Maybe not always before the first bite, but once it starts, it can feel like it takes over in a way that’s hard to explain without sounding ridiculous. I can be standing there thinking, very clearly, “Stop. You don’t need any more. Put it away.” And at the same time my hands are still going back for more food.

It’s like there are two parts of me. One part is watching it happen and knows I don’t want to keep doing it, and the other part just keeps moving—opening something else, taking another handful, going back to the kitchen again. I’m not sitting there calmly deciding, “Yes, I’d like more.” It feels more automatic than that.

And hunger isn’t really the point by then. Sometimes I’m not hungry, or I know I’ve had enough, but the need to keep eating sort of fills up my attention. I can tell myself I’ll stop after this one thing, and then almost immediately I’m reaching again. That’s honestly what bothers me the most and what brings me in—feeling like I can see myself doing it and I’m telling myself to stop, but I don’t actually stop.

When you’re in the middle of one of these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you’re completely unable to resist the urge to keep eating, even though you’re aware of trying to stop and you know you don’t want to continue?

Yes. I mean, “completely unable” is a hard phrase, because part of me feels like I should be able to stop. I’m awake, I know what I’m doing, I’m not confused about it. But in the moment it really does feel like I’m watching myself continue while I’m also telling myself not to.

That’s actually a big part of why I’m here. Once I start eating at night, it can feel like my mind is saying, “Enough, stop, you don’t want this,” but my hands just keep going back for more. I’ll put something away and then take it back out, or I’ll tell myself that was the last bite and then I’m reaching again almost right away. It doesn’t feel like a normal choice at that point.

So, yes, I’m aware I don’t want to continue, and I’m aware I’m trying to stop. But the urge keeps winning, at least for a while. It’s like I can see the whole thing happening and still not interrupt it. That loss of control is what scares me, honestly.
Do these nighttime eating episodes involve eating much more rapidly than normal, eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or eating large amounts of food when you’re not physically hungry?

Yes… definitely the large amount part. I’m not always paying attention to the speed, but some evenings it’s just way beyond what I would ever consider a normal meal.

Like, I might start with leftovers, and at first I can tell myself it’s just a little something because it’s there. But then it turns into a sandwich, then maybe cereal, then cookies, then I’m looking through the pantry for chips or crackers or whatever snack food is around. And by the time I step back and look at it, it’s… it’s far more than I’d ever put on a plate for supper and sit down in front of someone with.

It’s not like I planned to eat all of that. It sort of piles up in stages. One thing leads to another, and I keep telling myself each thing is the last thing. But added together, yes, it’s a lot. More than I need, and more than I’m comfortable admitting sometimes.

That’s actually a big part of why I’m here. Once I start eating at night, it can feel like my mind is saying, “Enough, stop, you don’t want this,” but my hands just keep going back for more. I’ll put something away and then take it back out, or I’ll tell myself that was the last bite and then I’m reaching again almost right away. It doesn’t feel like a normal choice at that point.

So, yes, I’m aware I don’t want to continue, and I’m aware I’m trying to stop. But the urge keeps winning, at least for a while. It’s like I can see the whole thing happening and still not interrupt it. That loss of control is what scares me, honestly.

inference.note: This turn supports the presence of a loss of control and an irresistible urge to eat at night, which aligns with F50.01 (Binge Eating Disorder). However, the patient does not report clear compensatory behaviors such as purging or fasting, ruling out F50.00 (Anorexia Nervosa) and F50.2 (Bulimia Nervosa). The emergence of features that suggest a possible eating disorder not otherwise specified or Night Eating Syndrome (F50.7) has been added due to the nocturnal pattern and lack of full criteria for other eating disorders.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences a loss of control over eating without the presence of binge eating episodes, which would help distinguish Night Eating Syndrome (F50.7) from Anorexia Nervosa, Binge-Eating/Purging Type (F50.01).
doctor.question: Do these nighttime eating episodes involve eating much more rapidly than normal, eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or eating large amounts of food when you’re not physically hungry?

target_item.name: Eating_Large_Amount
target_item.manifestation: Some evenings I’ll start with leftovers and end up eating sandwiches, cereal, cookies, and whatever snack food is in the pantry, far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal supper.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the nighttime episodes include consuming unusually large amounts of food, which directly matches this symptom item.

patient.answer:
Yes… definitely the large amount part. I’m not always paying attention to the speed, but some evenings it’s just way beyond what I would ever consider a normal meal.

Like, I might start with leftovers, and at first I can tell myself it’s just a little something because it’s there. But then it turns into a sandwich, then maybe cereal, then cookies, then I’m looking through the pantry for chips or crackers or whatever snack food is around. And by the time I step back and look at it, it’s… it’s far more than I’d ever put on a plate for supper and sit down in front of someone with.

It’s not like I planned to eat all of that. It sort of piles up in stages. One thing leads to another, and I keep telling myself each thing is the last thing. But added together, yes, it’s a lot. More than I need, and more than I’m comfortable admitting sometimes.

inference.note: The patient's description of nighttime eating episodes, loss of control, and inability to stop despite awareness and intention to stop supports Night Eating Syndrome (F50.7). There is insufficient evidence for F50.01 (Anorexia Nervosa) given the absence of restrictive eating, fear of weight gain, or body image disturbance.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits recurrent episodes of binge eating, characterized by eating large amounts of food rapidly, a sense of loss of control during the episodes, and continued eating despite a desire to stop. These behaviors are not better explained by another eating disorder or impulse control disorder, and the key features align with binge-eating disorder (F50.7).
